quotes.text: if you run out of work keep picking high value tasks. don't stop and wait for my input.
keep monitoring and don't stop. restart the monitor when it stops, that is your entire job. to keep this running.

fields.summary: With milestones 7 to 9 queued, the orchestrator planned milestone 10 under the owner's standing instruction to keep picking high-value work. It is the hand fixes the orchestrator still made while runs went unattended: a PR that conflicts after main moves sits in a wait step with no CI until a hand rhiza ship rebase (GitHub runs no CI on a conflicting PR, and ship check never reads mergeable); a flaky CI check fails the run, and the orchestrator reruns it and merges by hand; a daemon start that never journaled (disk full) blocks its change set until the daemon is restarted, because the unjournaled map never expires; the daemon keeps running an old binary after daemon code lands, until restarted by hand; and agent sessions sat on a Claude Code dialog for hours, found only by eye, although each session's hook status carries the time of its last tool call. Research agents traced each to its code: ship.go's pr view fields and checksVerdict, stepRunner.Holds dropping exit 75, daemonHeld's unjournaled map, ctx.Self and the flock lock (dropped on exec, so a re-exec is safe once no start is pending), and recordHook's Status.Hook.At.
fields.title: Milestone 10: runs heal themselves
